neighbours.label: timber or wood as a structural building material (timber framing, wooden beams), against stone and marble on the - pole
fire: The barn was rebuilt with heavy oak timber beams pegged together without nails.
Most cottages in the village have a timber frame infilled with wattle and daub.
The architect left the wooden rafters exposed above the open kitchen.
Builders used cross-laminated timber panels for all six floors of the new office.
The old chapel has a steep roof carried on carved wooden trusses.
Each wall of the cabin is made from spruce logs notched at the corners.
The porch rests on cedar posts and a deck of pine boards.
Engineers chose glued laminated timber for the arches of the station roof.
quiet: The barn was rebuilt with heavy granite blocks laid in lime mortar.
Most cottages in the village have thick walls of local flint and brick.
The architect left the concrete ceiling exposed above the open kitchen.
Builders used precast concrete slabs for all six floors of the new office.
The old chapel has a steep roof of slate laid over stone vaults.
Each wall of the cottage is made from limestone blocks squared at the corners.
The porch rests on brick piers and a floor of stone flags.
Engineers chose reinforced concrete for the arches of the station roof.

notes: Peaks: ' timber' x5, ' wooden' x3, ' wood', ' roof', 'r'after, ' horizontal' clapboard; the output promotes framing/joint/member/panel. The - pole is stone and marble materials ('made of bronze', 'marble, granite'), so the pole draws a timber-frame vs. masonry distinction. Near misses describe the same buildings in stone, brick or concrete.
